Zelensky:
During this year of war, we have received dozens, perhaps a few hundred, missiles to defend our skies.
Middle Eastern countries used about 2,000 in the first 48 hours of the war.
That doesn't mean we shouldn't support Middle Eastern allies. Of course we should support them, help them and defend them.
But everything has to be competitive.

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
Zelensky:
We told our American partners: Switch on Starlink in those parts of Russia where they launch ballistic missiles.
Why must we all be under attack? Why must all of Europe be afraid that Russian ballistic missiles will reach European territory?
Switch on Starlink. We will do it. We will handle it.
Of course, we will do it if Russia doesn't stop this war.
Switch it on. It's not difficult, really.

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
Zelensky:
Russia produces 140 ballistic missiles every month, and they already have 700 ballistic missiles in storage.
Everybody talks about these missiles, but you can solve this problem.
About 70% of the components in each ballistic missile come from other countries — Asia, the United States and Europe.
You can stop it because these are your companies. Worldwide companies are selling these components to Russia.

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
Zelensky:
Some countries think they need to keep their interceptors for themselves. They are ready to help Ukraine, but first they need to defend themselves.
But that will not help if Ukraine falls, if Russia breaks our defensive lines.
Nobody can defend themselves alone against a country that is ready to do anything, that is ready to kill ordinary civilians with missiles and drones.
They already have an army of around 2 million. There is no European country with an army that strong. European armies are not ready for such a struggle.

🇮🇷Tehran prepares to strike undersea cables if US-Israeli attacks resume - report
The attacks would be aimed at underwater communications cable in the Persian Gulf region, Reuters claims, citing two unnamed Iranian security officials.
"If Iran is attacked, there will be no more red lines... from undersea cables to military bases, including covert ones," one of the officials said as quoted by the media agency.
The officials pointed out that Iran has full access to the cables and warned the US not to “play with fire.”
Earlier this week, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps pointedly [warned](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76498) that “seven major internet cables run beneath the Strait of Hormuz.”
Iranian Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei also warned that Iran could target undersea internet cables, data centers, and AI facilities linked to the US if hostilities are resumed.

events.text:
💵 Brent near $114 as attacks on Saudi energy sites sustain risk premium
Brent crude traded around $113.75 a barrel on Friday, on track for a third consecutive weekly gain, after Houthi strikes on Saudi infrastructure kept a geopolitical risk premium firmly in place.
👉 The attacks have targeted key Saudi sites in recent days, including King Fahd International Airport in Dammam and the Shaybah oilfield, with the Gulf Cooperation Council reporting casualties and material damage. Houthi forces also claimed strikes on Riyadh's Defense Ministry, [Aramco's Yanbu facility and Abha airport](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76611). 
Analysts say the market is pricing in the risk of further disruption to Middle Eastern energy flows, with attention also on the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab el-Mandeb.
